newsitem.title: USA: Dade County's Ed Marquez is new Miami City Manager.
newsitem.headline: Dade County's Ed Marquez is new Miami City Manager.

text.p: Miami City Commission unanimously endorsed Dade County Finance Director Ed Marquez as the new Miami City Manager on Friday.

Marquez, 43, has been the county's finance director for 10 years, overseeing Dade bond issues and keeping track of the county's $4 billion budget. He is a certified public accountant who began his career with Dade County in 1977 as an auditor and later became county controller.
As city manager, he will guide Miami's efforts to close a $68 million gap in its $275 million budget for the year that began Oct 1.
"The problem is huge. It's very daunting," Marequez said Friday. However, he said, "I'm up to the task."
Marquez is among the corporte and public finance volunteers already helping the city draft a bail-out plan, which will include a $10 million loan from Dade County.
Marquez replaces City Manager Cesar Odio, who resigned to face federal charges of conspiracy and embezzlement in connection with city contracts.
Acting City Manager Merret Stierheim, a former Dade County manager who now heads the Greater Miami Convention and Visitors Bureau, is expected to step down from the interim post Nov 15.
